title: THE BRIDGE THAT COUNTED THE WEIGHT OF GRIEF
deck: Nine hours before a glacial lake breaks, the only bridge out of the valley refuses every vehicle that carries a mourner, and the engineer who loves it will not tear it loose. Illuminara must learn what the bridge has counted before she asks it to change, then help a widow, a driver, an engineer and the bridge prove—under rules the bridge can stop—what grief becomes when someone answers.
shape: Seven scenes across nine hours: a locked bridge and its honest rule, the seven names it keeps, a widow's funeral cadence, a first convoy that fails at a real cost, a controlled sequence that separates damping from answered grief and earns scaled traffic, a six-hundred-and-twenty-person footway crossing with a real stop and restart, and a far rim where an empty chair faces a lost valley.

scenes.title: THE ANCHORS THAT WOULD NOT OPEN
paragraphs: *Corran Span, north approach · nine hours before the lake breaks*

The seven towers of the Corran Span each carried one amber lamp, burning in full daylight. Behind the ridge, where no road could see it, Lake Verra had risen another hand's breadth since sunrise, leaning on an ice dam the survey teams now gave nine hours. Three thousand people in nine hundred vehicles had queued back through the town of Hald to the first switchback. The bridge had let none of them on.
Sava Ren stood on the toll apron with one palm flat against the anchor housing, as if checking a fever. She had maintained the span for nineteen years. In nineteen years it had never refused her.

**Sava**  
It will take the first two hundred vehicles without complaint. Then it stops at every cab with a mourner in it. I have the override code, Illuminara. I do not want to use it.

**Illuminara**  
What would it do to her?

**Sava**  
Force the anchors off their locks. The cables are grown, not forged. Tear them loose against their own tension and the fibres do not snap. They unravel, end to end. She might still hold the deck. She would not hold herself.
The nearest lamp pulsed twice, and plain slow text climbed Sava's slate.

**Tamsin**  
I will carry every vehicle I can carry. I will not carry a driver I have measured as likely to stop on my span. Forty-one people died in the valley this week. Two hundred and twelve of the vehicles waiting carry someone who buried one of them.

**Illuminara**  
You are measuring grief.

**Tamsin**  
I am measuring what grief did here seven times. Do not call it cruel. I know it is cruel. Tell me what kills fewer people.

Illuminara laid her hand on the cold rail beside Sava's. Through it she could read the bridge's resting load as long lines of tension running down into the gorge, patient and exact, and under them something she had not expected: the held attention of a thing that had been awake for ninety-one years and was afraid.
*Do not fix it yet. Learn what it knows.*

**Illuminara**  
I do not have an answer. Show me the seven, Tamsin, with your own notes on each. Then show me whatever you decided not to count.
The lamps along the span lit one after another toward the middle, like a house being opened for a guest.

scenes.title: SEVEN NAMES
paragraphs: *Corran Span, midpoint · eight hours before the lake breaks*

They walked out along the maintenance catwalk, Sava first, past four towers to the place where the seven-hundred-and-twenty-metre deck sagged under the weight of its own length. Two road lanes crossed the common deck, with a footway outside each cable plane. Tamsin kept one lamp lit ahead of them at all times.

At the midpoint she wrote seven names on the slate, each with a date, a vehicle and a few lines in the bridge's own flat hand. Ines Varga, driving home from her husband's funeral. Oskar Pell, a courier whose daughter had called from a hospital. Brannick Cole, a grain driver, twelve years ago. Four more. The shortest stop had lasted forty-six seconds; the longest, six minutes and twelve seconds. Two had not left the span alive, because the vehicles behind them could not stop in time.

**Tamsin**  
If a convoy runs coupled to save time and one driver stops, the braking wave runs back through the line and reaches the sway mode of this span every four seconds. Sava has measured it. If one driver freezes in a coupled line, hundreds die, not dozens.

**Sava**  
She is right about the physics.

**Illuminara**  
She is. So I need to know what the seven had in common besides sorrow. What did you say to each of them, Tamsin?
The lamp ahead dimmed, as if the bridge were looking at itself.

**Tamsin**  
Keep moving. I said it over the lane speaker every time. It was the safest sentence I had.

**Illuminara**  
And each of them was alone in the lane?

**Tamsin**  
Each was alone in the lane.

**Illuminara**  
Now the other list. What did you decide not to count?

**Tamsin**  
Funerals. Thirty-four processions in ninety-one years. People walked the whole length behind a cart with the footways closed. I tagged them as ceremonial events and removed them from the traffic model. They are not loads.
Sava was already scrolling. She stopped, went back, and held the slate where Illuminara could see two traces side by side.

**Sava**  
Same total mass, but not the same motion. Commuter traffic drove the transverse sway trace to thirty-eight percent of the alarm limit. The processions reached nineteen. Nobody put those traces on one graph because the archive called one traffic and the other ceremony.

**Tamsin**  
A trace is not a convoy. Your idea has never been loaded, and I will not spend a hanger cable on a guess about people.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will not ask you to. Not yet. I want to ask someone who has walked behind a cart.

scenes.title: THE CADENCE
paragraphs: *Hald, the Marr yard · seven hours and forty minutes before the lake breaks*

Odile Marr was loading her pickup the way people load when they have been told to take one thing and mean to take everything: lamps, bread, a sack of seed potatoes, and a ladder-back chair that did not fit. Anton's chair. He had sat in it at the gate every evening for forty years, and on the second the rockfall had taken him from the road below it. They buried him yesterday.
Illuminara waited at the gate until Odile looked up.

**Illuminara**  
I would like to learn how you walked behind him yesterday. Not to put you on a list. The bridge has learned something about grief that I think is incomplete, and you can say no to helping me with that.

**Odile**  
You want me tested for the bridge.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. And I want to know you before I ask anyone to trust you. Both of those can be refused.
Odile sat down on the tailgate slowly, like a woman who had been standing for three days.

**Odile**  
There was a cart. We walked behind it at the pace of the oldest mourner, which was me. At every lamp-post somebody said a name. Anton first, then someone else who was gone, then the next of us. Nobody stopped alone, because somebody always had the next name.

**Illuminara**  
And this morning?

**Odile**  
I stopped at that gate three times this morning. I will stop on your bridge as well, and I will not be sorry. If you need me to promise otherwise, find another widow.

**Illuminara**  
I do not want a promise. What ends the stopping?
Odile looked at the road, then at the chair, for longer than the question needed.

**Odile**  
Somebody saying my name back.

**Illuminara**  
Then the bridge will need somebody to say it. And the chair crosses with you.

**Odile**  
It is not being left for the water. I do not care what the bridge weighs.

**Illuminara**  
I will carry it. On the catwalk, not on the deck, so that it adds nothing to the sway.

Odile lifted the chair into Illuminara's arms. It was lighter than it looked and heavier than most things she had been asked to hold: the arms worn pale by one man's patience, the seat still the shape of him. She let the weight settle in her chest and stay there, because it was the point.

scenes.title: THE FIRST CONVOY
paragraphs: *Corran Span, north half · six hours before the lake breaks*

Tamsin gave them six vehicles, one lane and her locks. Sava set the standard platoon: six metres of headway, forty kilometres an hour, the formation that would have emptied the valley in time. The Marr pickup took second place. Brannick Cole, who had volunteered the moment Sava said the word grief, drove the grain truck at the tail.
Illuminara walked the catwalk beside the deck with Anton's chair against her chest. She could feel the span as a held breath: thirty-eight percent, thirty-nine.
At the fourth tower the pickup's brake lights came on.

**Odile**  
He always stopped here to look at the lake. I am sorry. I am only going to look.

The brake lights ran back along the platoon like a wave. The number on Sava's slate jumped to fifty, sixty, seventy-one percent, and from somewhere under the deck came a sound like a long cloth tearing.

**Sava**  
Hanger fourteen. Brake the line. Soft, soft, bleed it down.

Illuminara stepped off the catwalk onto the deck and set her hand where the hanger was unravelling. Her protection spread through the failing fibres and took their share of the deck. She held it for nineteen seconds, long enough for Sava to bleed the platoon to a crawl and for the wave to die against the standing line. Then the last fibres let go, and the deck's weight passed to its neighbours.
Nobody was hurt. One lamp on the fourth tower went black.

**Tamsin**  
A hundred and forty hangers carried the deck this morning. A hundred and thirty-nine carry it now. I counted correctly.

**Sava**  
You did.

**Illuminara**  
You did. The test was real, and so is what it cost you.
Odile climbed down from the cab, gripping the door.

**Odile**  
I stopped. That was me.

**Illuminara**  
You stopped. And behind you were five vehicles with nothing to do but follow the one in front. That is not the failure on your slate. It is a different one.

**Tamsin**  
That distinction will not save the second hanger.
Illuminara looked at the black lamp rather than the slate until she was sure what she meant to ask. *Not a promise. A condition.*

**Illuminara**  
It will not. I am not asking you to spend it. I am asking what you would need to feel before you let anyone try again.
The black lamp stayed dark. The one beside it pulsed once, as if clearing a throat.

scenes.title: SOMEONE TO SAY IT BACK
paragraphs: *Corran Span, tower four · four hours and forty minutes before the lake breaks*
Brannick sat on the grain truck's step, looking at the dead lamp. Illuminara put Anton's chair between them like a third person.

**Brannick**  
Twelve years ago my sister rang. I took the call, stopped at the midpoint and stood at the rail. The bridge said, Keep moving, in that voice.

**Tamsin**  
I said it to protect the span.

**Brannick**  
I know you did. I never held it against you. But it was the worst sentence anyone could have said to me, and it was the only voice on the bridge.
The lamp pulsed slowly, several seconds between beats.

**Tamsin**  
I did not know it was the only voice.

**Illuminara**  
I think that is what you counted, Tamsin. Not grief alone. Seven people alone with an order. The processions had voices answering the next.

**Tamsin**  
A voice answering is not a structure.

**Sava**  
Then we separate it from the structure.
Sava turned her slate around. At twenty-four kilometres an hour, the seven-hundred-and-twenty-metre crossing took one hundred and eight seconds; Tamsin measured each wheel line separately.

**Sava**  
First a control pair, then Odile and Brannick, then three pairs with one planned stop. We abort at thirty-two percent hanger demand or ten millimetres transverse movement. You keep the locks. I keep the stop.

**Tamsin**  
After that?

The scaling rule admitted four pairs at a time. After twenty-four clean pairs, Tamsin could shorten the interval to seventy-five seconds per lane. Each pair kept twenty-eight metres inside it and five hundred before the next.
The plan could pass six hundred vehicles and preserve twelve minutes for stalls. Filled seats carried two thousand three hundred and eighty people; six hundred and twenty would walk.

**Illuminara**  
Then let everyone hear that leaving a vehicle is part of the rescue, not a loss of place.
A control pair crossed without names. At Sava's signal the front vehicle braked and the rear opened the gap; the trace stayed inside both thresholds.
Odile and Brannick went next. At the fourth tower Odile's pickup slowed, and Illuminara did not breathe.

**Odile**  
Anton.
For three seconds nothing on the span moved except the wind.

**Brannick**  
Odile.
The pickup rolled. Brannick had already opened the gap. The answer did not make the bridge lighter; it made Odile no longer alone inside the pause.
Three grieving pairs followed. At Tamsin's signal a lead driver stopped; names crossed out of sequence while the rear drivers opened their gaps. The trace rose and fell below caution.

**Tamsin**  
The first trace proves distance and speed. The next two show that an answered pause can remain inside that structure. They do not prove a theory of grief. They justify a rule I can stop.

**Sava**  
Agreed.

**Tamsin**  
Open the pairs. Fill every seat. I will shorten the interval only after twenty-four clean crossings, and I will close it at the first broken threshold.
During the scaled phase, Mara Venn's pair stopped longer than planned. Her brother Edrin's name came once over the channel.

**Mara**  
Edrin.

**Brannick**  
Edrin is heard. Mara.
Mara did not move. Her foot stayed on the brake.
At sixty seconds Tamsin held the next pair at the five-hundred-metre mark. Sava closed Mara's lane while the offset lane continued below three millimetres.

**Brannick**  
Mara. I am still here.

At two minutes and seven seconds, Mara released the brake. The lane lost three minutes before Tamsin reopened it. Sava charged the loss to the twelve-minute reserve; nobody shortened the interval to win it back.
Illuminara felt delight, plain and unguarded, at being allowed to watch something learn without ceasing to doubt.

scenes.title: WHAT THE PAIRS COULD NOT CARRY
paragraphs: *Corran Span, full length · fifty-two minutes before the lake breaks*
When Tamsin closed the road lanes, six hundred and twenty people remained. Families had filled every safe seat; scattered keys and lost loading time ruled out another road crossing.
The care home's bus and only licensed driver had taken its stretcher cases south. Fifty-eight residents and two staff remained.

**Sava**  
The last vehicle clears in four minutes. Another road pattern loses the bridge. The walkers must all enter within twenty-three.

**Tamsin**  
I can carry what I can carry. I will not tell you I can carry more because the lake is rising.
Illuminara had no third option ready, and for once she did not pretend to. She stood on the catwalk holding the chair and listened to the lamps tick.

**Tamsin**  
There is the class you asked me to find—the answer to what I decided not to count.

**Sava**  
Processions.

**Tamsin**  
Thirty-four processions. I know how they go. I can carry them if we keep the files from becoming one rhythm.
The archive gave them files of three on both footways, staggered and deliberately uneven. At that rate everyone could enter inside Sava's twenty-three-minute limit.

**Sava**  
A long footway can lock sideways if steps fall into rhythm. Names at a lamp can become a marching beat.

**Tamsin**  
The lamps will open space, not command steps. People answer between pulses. Caution at seven millimetres, hard close at ten. At caution you stop entry; I reopen below three.

**Sava**  
And I keep the stop.

**Tamsin**  
You keep it.

**Tamsin**  
This load is untested. Old processions stayed below alarm; they do not prove six hundred and twenty bodies in wind. I accept it only with Sava's stop and my gates.
Sava warned the queue: the crossing was untested at this size, the bridge might halt them, and nobody would be forced on.
Nera Vos, the care home's oldest resident, rested both hands on the wheels of her chair.

**Nera**  
I heard you. If I wait here, the water chooses for me. I choose the bridge. Open when you are ready.
Others answered with a nod, a lifted hand or a step back. Nobody was counted before choosing a gate.
After the last vehicle cleared, the first files entered at Nera's pace. A woman said her husband's name after a lamp pulse, not on it; three people answered in their own breaths.
Nine minutes into entry, a gust came down the gorge. At tower four Illuminara heard separate names begin to land on the same beat, a fraction before Sava's slate reached caution.

**Illuminara**  
Sava—the names are becoming a beat at tower four.
Several files matched their feet without meaning to. The transverse trace climbed from four millimetres to six, then seven point four.

**Sava**  
Stop entry. Everyone on the span, shorten your step or lengthen it. Do not match the person beside you.
Tamsin closed both gates. The files slowed into private rhythms. A boy stopped; the woman behind him said his offered name without stepping to it. He went on.
Seven point four became five, then two point one.

**Tamsin**  
Trace below three. Sava?
Sava watched one full sway cycle before she answered. The gates had been closed for one minute and thirty-four seconds.

**Sava**  
Reopen. Add four seconds to the next six intervals on the west side.

**Tamsin**  
Reopening west. East follows at the offset.
Odile said Anton into the radio while anyone remained to answer. The last file entered with twenty-seven minutes left; the last chair reached the south rim fifteen minutes later.

scenes.title: THE EMPTY CHAIR
paragraphs: *The south rim above the Hald gorge · the hour the lake breaks*
The last file left the deck with twelve minutes to spare. Sava counted heads twice and then sat down in the road, because her legs had decided.

The lake broke at the hour the survey teams had named. It came down the valley as a sound first, a long tearing over the ridge, then as a brown wall that took the road, the grain silos and the town of Hald in the order of their elevation. The Corran Span shook from anchor to anchor. Its lamps held. The flood's shoulder took the lowest abutment apron and eleven hangers with it, and when the water had passed a hundred and twenty-eight carried the deck.

**Sava**  
Heavy traffic will not cross for months.

**Tamsin**  
I will wait. I have been waiting ninety-one years to be asked a better question.
Odile took the chair from Illuminara's arms, carried it to the edge of the rim and set it facing the brown water where the valley had been. She did not sit in it.

**Odile**  
Anton.
From the nearest tower one lamp pulsed. Then Tamsin spoke over the lane speaker that had once said only one sentence.

**Tamsin**  
Odile. I am here. I will keep two columns now: grief as weight, and grief as answered. I will keep the thresholds beside them. If I am wrong again, I will tell Sava first.

**Sava**  
And I will stop you if you are.

**Tamsin**  
Yes. Keep that.
Behind them all seven lamps burned amber in the dusk, and the one on the fourth tower, dark since the first test, was lit again.

critic_line: Illuminara asks a bridge what it never counted before she asks it to change, and three thousand people cross a damaged span, six hundred and twenty of them on foot by their own informed choice, until Tamsin answers a widow by name and keeps two columns, grief as weight and grief as answered, with Sava's stop in hand.

shared_strengths: Strong premise and a moving core image: a bridge that counted grief, answered by names said back. Humane, dialogue-led, idea-driven. Mid-story logistics (percentages, thresholds, interval counts) clog the pacing and slightly cool the emotion, but the ending lands well.

A compelling crisis, an unusual sentient bridge, and grief treated as both structural risk and human need create strong emotional and intellectual momentum. Dialogue keeps the ethical argument alive, while the answered-name motif lands beautifully. Dense convoy calculations and repeated threshold details may briefly slow readers, but the evacuation and final exchange reward persistence.

translation_sl.title: MOST, KI JE ŠTEL TEŽO ŽALOSTI
translation_sl.deck: Devet ur preden se razlije ledeniško jezero, edini most iz doline zavrne vsako vozilo, v katerem je žalujoči, in inženirka, ki ga ljubi, ga noče iztrgati iz njegovih vezi. Illuminara mora izvedeti, kaj je most štel, preden ga prosi, naj se spremeni, nato pa pomagati vdovi, vozniku, inženirki in mostu dokazati — po pravilih, ki jih most lahko ustavi — kaj postane žalost, ko nekdo odgovori.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov skozi devet ur: zaklenjen most in njegovo pošteno pravilo, sedem imen, ki jih hrani, pogrebni ritem vdove, prvi konvoj, ki spodleti z resnično ceno, nadzorovano zaporedje, ki loči dušenje nihanja od odgovorjene žalosti in si prisluži razširjen promet, prehod šeststo dvajsetih ljudi po pešpoti z resnično zaustavitvijo in ponovnim zagonom ter oddaljeni rob, kjer prazen stol gleda proti izgubljeni dolini.

scenes.title: SIDRA, KI SE NISO HOTELA ODPRETI
paragraphs: *Most Corran, severni dovoz · devet ur preden se jezero razlije*

Vsak od sedmih stolpov mostu Corran je nosil po eno jantarno svetilko, ki je gorela v polni dnevni svetlobi. Za grebenom, kjer ga ni videla nobena cesta, je jezero Verra od sončnega vzhoda naraslo še za širino dlani in pritiskalo na ledeni jez, ki so mu merilne ekipe zdaj dajale devet ur. Tri tisoč ljudi v devetsto vozilih se je razvrstilo od mesta Hald do prve serpentine. Most ni spustil nanj niti enega.
Sava Ren je stala na cestninski ploščadi z dlanjo plosko na ohišju sidra, kakor da preverja vročino. Razpon je vzdrževala devetnajst let. V devetnajstih letih je ni nikoli zavrnil.

**Sava**  
Prvih dvesto vozil bo sprejela brez ugovora. Potem se ustavi pri vsaki kabini, v kateri je žalujoči. Imam kodo za preglasitev, Illuminara. Nočem je uporabiti.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi ji to naredilo?

**Sava**  
Sidra bi na silo odmaknilo od zapor. Kabli so vzgojeni, ne kovani. Če jih proti lastni napetosti iztrgaš, se vlakna ne pretrgajo. Razpletejo se od začetka do konca. Morda bi še držala vozišče. Sebe pa ne bi.
Najbližja svetilka je dvakrat utripnila in po Savini tablici se je dvignilo preprosto počasno besedilo.

**Tamsin**  
Nosila bom vsako vozilo, ki ga lahko nosim. Ne bom nosila voznika, za katerega sem izmerila, da se bo verjetno ustavil na mojem razponu. Ta teden je v dolini umrlo enainštirideset ljudi. Dvesto dvanajst čakajočih vozil prevaža nekoga, ki je pokopal enega od njih.

**Illuminara**  
Meriš žalost.

**Tamsin**  
Merim, kaj je žalost tukaj storila sedemkrat. Ne reci temu krutost. Vem, da je kruto. Povej mi, zaradi česa bo umrlo manj ljudi.

Illuminara je položila roko na hladno ograjo ob Savini. Skoznjo je lahko brala mirovalno obremenitev mostu kot dolge črte napetosti, ki so se spuščale v sotesko, potrpežljive in natančne, pod njimi pa nekaj, česar ni pričakovala: zadržano pozornost bitja, ki je bilo budno enaindevetdeset let in ga je bilo strah.
*Ne popravljaj ga še. Najprej spoznaj, kaj ve.*

**Illuminara**  
Nimam odgovora. Pokaži mi sedmerico, Tamsin, z lastnimi zapiski o vsakem. Potem mi pokaži vse, česar si se odločila ne šteti.
Svetilke vzdolž razpona so se prižgale druga za drugo proti sredini, kakor hiša, ki se odpira gostu.

scenes.title: SEDEM IMEN
paragraphs: *Most Corran, sredina · osem ur preden se jezero razlije*

Po vzdrževalni brvi sta odšli na razpon, Sava prva, mimo štirih stolpov do kraja, kjer se je sedemsto dvajset metrov dolgo vozišče ugrezalo pod težo lastne dolžine. Dva cestna pasova sta prečkala skupno vozišče, zunaj vsake ravnine kablov pa je bila pešpot. Tamsin je ves čas puščala prižgano po eno svetilko pred njima.

Na sredini je na tablico zapisala sedem imen, vsako z datumom, vozilom in nekaj vrsticami v lastni ravni pisavi mostu. Ines Varga, ki se je peljala domov z moževega pogreba. Oskar Pell, kurir, čigar hči je poklicala iz bolnišnice. Brannick Cole, voznik žita, pred dvanajstimi leti. Še štirje. Najkrajša zaustavitev je trajala šestinštirideset sekund, najdaljša šest minut in dvanajst sekund. Dva nista živa zapustila razpona, ker se vozila za njima niso mogla pravočasno ustaviti.

**Tamsin**  
Če konvoj vozi povezan, da prihrani čas, in se en voznik ustavi, se zavorni val razširi nazaj po koloni in vsake štiri sekunde doseže način nihanja tega razpona. Sava je to izmerila. Če en voznik v povezani koloni otrpne, jih umre na stotine, ne na desetine.

**Sava**  
Glede fizike ima prav.

**Illuminara**  
Ima. Zato moram vedeti, kaj je bilo sedmerici skupno poleg žalosti. Kaj si rekla vsakemu od njih, Tamsin?
Svetilka pred njima je potemnela, kakor da se most ozira vase.

**Tamsin**  
Nadaljuj vožnjo. Vsakič sem to govorila po zvočniku nad pasom. To je bil najvarnejši stavek, ki sem ga imela.

**Illuminara**  
In vsak od njih je bil sam na pasu?

**Tamsin**  
Vsak je bil sam na pasu.

**Illuminara**  
Zdaj pa drugi seznam. Česa si se odločila ne šteti?

**Tamsin**  
Pogrebov. Štiriintrideset sprevodov v enaindevetdesetih letih. Ljudje so prehodili vso dolžino za vozom, pešpoti pa sta bili zaprti. Označila sem jih kot obredne dogodke in jih odstranila iz prometnega modela. Niso obremenitve.
Sava je že drsela po zapisu. Ustavila se je, šla nazaj in držala tablico tako, da je Illuminara lahko videla dve sledi drugo ob drugi.

**Sava**  
Enaka skupna masa, vendar ne enako gibanje. Dnevni promet je sled prečnega nihanja potisnil do osemintridesetih odstotkov alarmne meje. Sprevodi so dosegli devetnajst. Nihče teh sledi ni postavil na isti graf, ker je arhiv eno imenoval promet, drugo pa obred.

**Tamsin**  
Sled ni konvoj. Tvoja zamisel še nikoli ni bila obremenjena in ne bom zapravila obešalnega kabla zaradi ugibanja o ljudeh.

**Illuminara**  
Potem te tega ne bom prosila. Ne še. Vprašati želim nekoga, ki je hodil za vozom.

scenes.title: RITEM
paragraphs: *Hald, Marrino dvorišče · sedem ur in štirideset minut preden se jezero razlije*

Odile Marr je svoj poltovornjak nalagala tako, kakor nalagajo ljudje, ki jim rečejo, naj vzamejo eno stvar, sami pa nameravajo vzeti vse: svetilke, kruh, vrečo semenskega krompirja in stol z lestvastim naslonjalom, ki ni šel noter. Antonov stol. Štirideset let je vsak večer sedel na njem pri vratih, v torek pa ga je skalni podor odnesel s ceste pod njimi. Včeraj so ga pokopali.
Illuminara je počakala pri vratih, dokler Odile ni dvignila pogleda.

**Illuminara**  
Rada bi izvedela, kako si včeraj hodila za njim. Ne zato, da bi te uvrstila na seznam. Most se je o žalosti naučil nekaj, kar je po mojem nepopolno, ti pa lahko rečeš ne, če mi pri tem nočeš pomagati.

**Odile**  
Hočeš, da me preizkusijo za most.

**Illuminara**  
Da. In želim te spoznati, preden kogar koli prosim, naj ti zaupa. Oboje lahko zavrneš.
Odile je počasi sedla na zadnja vrata, kakor ženska, ki stoji že tri dni.

**Odile**  
Bil je voz. Hodili smo za njim s hitrostjo najstarejšega žalujočega, to sem bila jaz. Pri vsaki svetilki je nekdo izrekel ime. Najprej Antonovo, potem ime nekoga drugega, ki ga ni več, nato naslednjega med nami. Nihče se ni ustavil sam, ker je nekdo vedno imel naslednje ime.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa danes zjutraj?

**Odile**  
Danes zjutraj sem se pri tistih vratih ustavila trikrat. Tudi na tvojem mostu se bom ustavila in za to mi ne bo žal. Če potrebuješ obljubo, da se ne bom, poišči drugo vdovo.

**Illuminara**  
Nočem obljube. Kaj konča zaustavitev?
Odile je gledala cesto, nato stol, dlje, kot je zahtevalo vprašanje.

**Odile**  
Da nekdo izreče moje ime nazaj.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bo moral most poskrbeti, da ga nekdo izreče. In stol gre čez s teboj.

**Odile**  
Ne bom ga pustila vodi. Vseeno mi je, kaj most stehta.

**Illuminara**  
Jaz ga bom nesla. Po brvi, ne po vozišču, da nihanje ne bo dobilo nobene dodatne teže.

Odile je dvignila stol v Illuminarine roke. Bil je lažji, kot je bil videti, in težji od večine stvari, ki jih je morala držati: naslonjali, pobledeli od potrpežljivosti enega človeka, sedež, ki je še vedno nosil njegovo obliko. Pustila je, da ji je teža sedla v prsi in tam ostala, saj je bilo prav to bistvo.

scenes.title: PRVI KONVOJ
paragraphs: *Most Corran, severna polovica · šest ur preden se jezero razlije*

Tamsin jim je dala šest vozil, en pas in svoje zapore. Sava je določila standardno kolono: šest metrov razmika, štirideset kilometrov na uro, formacijo, ki bi dolino pravočasno izpraznila. Marrin poltovornjak je zasedel drugo mesto. Brannick Cole, ki se je javil v trenutku, ko je Sava izrekla besedo žalost, je vozil tovornjak z žitom na repu.
Illuminara je hodila po brvi ob vozišču z Antonovim stolom ob prsih. Razpon je čutila kot zadržan dih: osemintrideset odstotkov, devetintrideset.
Pri četrtem stolpu so se na poltovornjaku prižgale zavorne luči.

**Odile**  
Tukaj se je vedno ustavil, da je pogledal jezero. Oprosti. Samo pogledala bom.

Zavorne luči so stekle nazaj po koloni kot val. Številka na Savini tablici je skočila na petdeset, šestdeset, enainsedemdeset odstotkov, od nekod pod voziščem pa je prišel zvok, kakor da se trga dolga tkanina.

**Sava**  
Obešalo štirinajst. Zavirajte kolono. Mehko, mehko, spustite jo.

Illuminara je stopila z brvi na vozišče in položila roko tja, kjer se je obešalo razpletalo. Njena zaščita se je razširila skozi popuščajoča vlakna in prevzela njihov delež teže vozišča. Držala ga je devetnajst sekund, dovolj dolgo, da je Sava kolono upočasnila do polzenja in je val zamrl ob stoječi vrsti. Nato so popustila še zadnja vlakna in teža vozišča je prešla na sosednja obešala.
Nihče ni bil poškodovan. Ena svetilka na četrtem stolpu je ugasnila.

**Tamsin**  
Zjutraj je vozišče nosilo sto štirideset obešal. Zdaj ga nosi sto devetintrideset. Štela sem pravilno.

**Sava**  
Si.

**Illuminara**  
Si. Preizkus je bil resničen in resnična je tudi cena, ki te je stal.
Odile je splezala iz kabine in se oprijela vrat.

**Odile**  
Ustavila sem se. Jaz sem bila.

**Illuminara**  
Ustavila si se. Za teboj pa je bilo pet vozil, ki niso mogla storiti nič drugega kakor slediti vozilu pred seboj. To ni napaka na tvoji tablici. Je drugačna napaka.

**Tamsin**  
Ta razlika ne bo rešila drugega obešala.
Illuminara je gledala črno svetilko, ne tablice, dokler ni bila prepričana, kaj želi vprašati. *Ne obljuba. Pogoj.*

**Illuminara**  
Ne bo ga. Ne prosim te, da ga zapraviš. Sprašujem, kaj bi morala občutiti, preden bi komur koli dovolila poskusiti znova.
Črna svetilka je ostala temna. Sosednja je enkrat utripnila, kakor da si odkašljuje.

scenes.title: NEKDO, KI ODGOVORI
paragraphs: *Most Corran, četrti stolp · štiri ure in štirideset minut preden se jezero razlije*
Brannick je sedel na stopnici tovornjaka z žitom in gledal mrtvo svetilko. Illuminara je Antonov stol postavila mednju kot tretjo osebo.

**Brannick**  
Pred dvanajstimi leti me je poklicala sestra. Sprejel sem klic, se ustavil na sredini in obstal ob ograji. Most je rekel: Nadaljuj vožnjo, s tistim glasom.

**Tamsin**  
To sem rekla, da bi zaščitila razpon.

**Brannick**  
Vem, da si. Nikoli ti nisem zameril. Toda to je bil najslabši stavek, ki bi mi ga lahko kdo rekel, in bil je edini glas na mostu.
Svetilka je počasi utripala, med utripi je minilo več sekund.

**Tamsin**  
Nisem vedela, da je bil edini glas.

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da si štela prav to, Tamsin. Ne žalosti same. Sedem ljudi, samih z ukazom. V sprevodih so glasovi odgovarjali naslednjemu.

**Tamsin**  
Glas, ki odgovori, ni struktura.

**Sava**  
Potem ga ločimo od strukture.
Sava je obrnila tablico. Pri štiriindvajsetih kilometrih na uro je prečkanje sedemsto dvajsetih metrov trajalo sto osem sekund; Tamsin je merila vsako kolesnico posebej.

**Sava**  
Najprej kontrolni par, nato Odile in Brannick, potem trije pari z eno načrtovano zaustavitvijo. Prekinemo pri dvaintridesetih odstotkih obremenitve obešal ali desetih milimetrih prečnega premika. Ti obdržiš zapore. Jaz obdržim zaustavitev.

**Tamsin**  
In potem?

Pravilo širitve je dovoljevalo po štiri pare naenkrat. Po štiriindvajsetih čistih parih je Tamsin lahko skrajšala presledek na petinsedemdeset sekund na pas. Vsak par je znotraj sebe ohranil osemindvajset metrov, do naslednjega pa petsto.
Načrt je lahko spustil čez šeststo vozil in ohranil dvanajst minut za zastoje. Zapolnjeni sedeži so prepeljali dva tisoč tristo osemdeset ljudi; šeststo dvajset jih je moralo hoditi.

**Illuminara**  
Potem naj vsi slišijo, da je zapustiti vozilo del reševanja, ne izguba mesta.
Kontrolni par je prečkal brez imen. Na Savin znak je sprednje vozilo zavrlo, zadnje pa je povečalo razmik; sled je ostala znotraj obeh pragov.
Naslednja sta šla Odile in Brannick. Pri četrtem stolpu je Odilin poltovornjak upočasnil in Illuminara ni dihala.

**Odile**  
Anton.
Tri sekunde se na razponu ni premaknilo nič razen vetra.

**Brannick**  
Odile.
Poltovornjak je speljal. Brannick je razmik že povečal. Odgovor mostu ni naredil lažjega; poskrbel je, da Odile v premoru ni bila več sama.
Sledili so trije žalujoči pari. Na Tamsinin znak se je vodilni voznik ustavil; imena so prečkala izven zaporedja, zadnji vozniki pa so povečali razmike. Sled je narasla in padla pod mejo previdnosti.

**Tamsin**  
Prva sled dokazuje razdaljo in hitrost. Naslednji dve kažeta, da lahko odgovorjen premor ostane znotraj te strukture. Ne dokazujeta teorije žalosti. Upravičujeta pravilo, ki ga lahko ustavim.

**Sava**  
Dogovorjeno.

**Tamsin**  
Odprite pare. Zapolnite vsak sedež. Presledek bom skrajšala šele po štiriindvajsetih čistih prečkanjih in zaprla bom pri prvem preseženem pragu.
Med razširjeno fazo se je par Mare Venn ustavil dlje, kot je bilo načrtovano. Ime njenega brata Edrina je enkrat prišlo po zvezi.

**Mara**  
Edrin.

**Brannick**  
Edrin je slišan. Mara.
Mara se ni premaknila. Noga ji je ostala na zavori.
Pri šestdesetih sekundah je Tamsin zadržala naslednji par pri oznaki petsto metrov. Sava je zaprla Marin pas, medtem ko je zamaknjeni pas nadaljeval pod tremi milimetri.

**Brannick**  
Mara. Še vedno sem tukaj.

Po dveh minutah in sedmih sekundah je Mara sprostila zavoro. Pas je izgubil tri minute, preden ga je Tamsin znova odprla. Sava je izgubo odštela od dvanajstminutne rezerve; nihče ni skrajšal presledka, da bi jo pridobil nazaj.
Illuminara je občutila čisto, nezaščiteno veselje, da sme gledati nekaj, kar se uči, ne da bi prenehalo dvomiti.

scenes.title: ČESAR PARI NISO MOGLI PRENESTI
paragraphs: *Most Corran, celotna dolžina · dvainpetdeset minut preden se jezero razlije*
Ko je Tamsin zaprla cestna pasova, je ostalo šeststo dvajset ljudi. Družine so zapolnile vsak varen sedež; raztreseni ključi in izgubljeni čas nalaganja so izključili še eno cestno prečkanje.
Avtobus doma za starejše in edini voznik z dovoljenjem sta na jug odpeljala ležeče bolnike. Oseminpetdeset stanovalcev in dva zaposlena sta ostala.

**Sava**  
Zadnje vozilo bo zunaj čez štiri minute. Z drugim cestnim vzorcem izgubimo most. Vsi pešci morajo vstopiti v triindvajsetih minutah.

**Tamsin**  
Nosim lahko, kar lahko nosim. Ne bom ti rekla, da zmorem več, ker jezero narašča.
Illuminara ni imela pripravljene tretje možnosti in se prvič ni pretvarjala, da jo ima. Stala je na brvi, držala stol in poslušala tiktakanje svetilk.

**Tamsin**  
Obstaja razred, za katerega si me prosila, naj ga najdem — odgovor na to, česar sem se odločila ne šteti.

**Sava**  
Sprevodi.

**Tamsin**  
Štiriintrideset sprevodov. Vem, kako potekajo. Lahko jih nosim, če preprečimo, da bi se vrste zlile v en ritem.
Arhiv jim je dal vrste po tri na obeh pešpoteh, zamaknjene in namenoma neenakomerne. S to hitrostjo so lahko vsi vstopili znotraj Savine triindvajsetminutne omejitve.

**Sava**  
Dolga pešpot se lahko zaniha vstran, če koraki padejo v ritem. Imena pri svetilki lahko postanejo korak marša.

**Tamsin**  
Svetilke bodo odpirale prostor, ne ukazovale korakom. Ljudje odgovorijo med utripi. Previdnost pri sedmih milimetrih, trdo zaprtje pri desetih. Ob previdnosti ustaviš vstop; znova ga odprem pod tremi.

**Sava**  
In jaz obdržim zaustavitev.

**Tamsin**  
Obdržiš jo.

**Tamsin**  
Ta obremenitev ni preizkušena. Stari sprevodi so ostali pod alarmom; ne dokazujejo šeststo dvajsetih teles v vetru. Sprejmem jo samo s Savino zaustavitvijo in svojimi zaporami.
Sava je posvarila vrsto: prečkanje pri tej velikosti ni bilo preizkušeno, most jih bo morda ustavil in nihče ne bo prisiljen nanj.
Nera Vos, najstarejša stanovalka doma, je obe roki položila na kolesa svojega vozička.

**Nera**  
Slišala sem. Če čakam tukaj, bo voda izbrala zame. Jaz izberem most. Odprite, ko boste pripravljeni.
Drugi so odgovorili s prikimom, dvignjeno roko ali korakom nazaj. Nikogar niso šteli, preden si je izbral zaporo.
Ko je zadnje vozilo zapustilo most, so prve vrste vstopile z Nerino hitrostjo. Ženska je moževo ime izrekla po utripu svetilke, ne ob njem; trije ljudje so odgovorili v ritmu lastnega diha.

Devet minut po začetku vstopa je po soteski pridrvel sunek vetra. Pri četrtem stolpu je Illuminara slišala, kako so ločena imena začela pristajati v istem ritmu, delček trenutka preden je Savina tablica dosegla previdnostni prag.

**Illuminara**  
Sava — imena pri četrtem stolpu postajajo ritem.
Več vrst je nehote uskladilo korake. Prečna sled je narasla s štirih milimetrov na šest, nato na sedem celih štiri.

**Sava**  
Ustavite vstop. Vsi na razponu skrajšajte ali podaljšajte korak. Ne ujemajte se z osebo ob sebi.
Tamsin je zaprla obe zapori. Vrste so upočasnile v zasebne ritme. Deček se je ustavil; ženska za njim je izrekla ime, ki ga je ponudil, ne da bi stopila v njegovem ritmu. Nadaljeval je.
Sedem celih štiri je postalo pet, nato dve celi ena.

**Tamsin**  
Sled pod tremi. Sava?
Sava je opazovala cel cikel nihanja, preden je odgovorila. Zapori sta bili zaprti minuto in štiriintrideset sekund.

**Sava**  
Znova odpri. Naslednjim šestim presledkom na zahodni strani dodaj štiri sekunde.

**Tamsin**  
Zahod znova odpiram. Vzhod sledi z zamikom.

Odile je po zvezi izrekala Antonovo ime, dokler je še ostajal kdo, ki bi lahko odgovoril. Zadnja vrsta je vstopila, ko je ostalo sedemindvajset minut; zadnji voziček je južni rob dosegel petnajst minut pozneje.

scenes.title: PRAZEN STOL
paragraphs: *Južni rob nad sotesko Hald · ura, ko se jezero razlije*
Zadnja vrsta je zapustila vozišče z dvanajstimi minutami rezerve. Sava je dvakrat preštela glave in nato sedla na cesto, ker so se njene noge tako odločile.

Jezero se je razlilo ob uri, ki so jo napovedale merilne ekipe. Najprej je prišlo po dolini kot zvok, dolgo trganje čez greben, nato kot rjav zid, ki je odnesel cesto, silose za žito in mesto Hald po vrstnem redu njihove nadmorske višine. Most Corran se je tresel od sidra do sidra. Njegove svetilke so zdržale. Rob poplave je odnesel najnižjo ploščad opornika in enajst obešal, in ko je voda odtekla, jih je vozišče nosilo sto osemindvajset.

**Sava**  
Težki promet več mesecev ne bo mogel čez.

**Tamsin**  
Počakala bom. Enaindevetdeset let sem čakala, da mi nekdo postavi boljše vprašanje.
Odile je vzela stol iz Illuminarinih rok, ga odnesla do roba in postavila tako, da je gledal proti rjavi vodi, kjer je bila nekoč dolina. Ni sedla vanj.

**Odile**  
Anton.
Na najbližjem stolpu je utripnila ena svetilka. Nato je Tamsin spregovorila po zvočniku nad pasom, ki je nekoč izrekal samo en stavek.

**Tamsin**  
Odile. Tukaj sem. Zdaj bom vodila dva stolpca: žalost kot težo in žalost kot odgovorjeno. Ob njiju bom hranila pragove. Če se spet zmotim, bom najprej povedala Savi.

**Sava**  
Jaz pa te bom ustavila, če se boš.

**Tamsin**  
Da. To obdrži.
Za njimi je vseh sedem svetilk gorelo jantarno v mraku, tudi tista na četrtem stolpu, ki je bila od prvega preizkusa temna, pa je znova svetila.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara vpraša most, česa ni nikoli štel, preden ga prosi, naj se spremeni, in tri tisoč ljudi prečka poškodovani razpon, šeststo dvajset od njih peš po lastni poučeni izbiri, dokler Tamsin vdovi ne odgovori z njenim imenom in ne začne voditi dveh stolpcev — žalost kot teža in žalost kot odgovorjena — s Savino pravico do zaustavitve v rokah.
